Tableside Baby Bananas Foster

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 10 min

Tableside Baby Bananas Foster is a dramatic and delightful dessert, perfect for a special occasion like the Childermas Banquet. Its warm, caramelized bananas and fiery presentation bring a sense of wonder and joy, making it a fitting sweet treat to celebrate the innocence and spirit of children during this reflective feast.

Ingredients

  • 4 tablespoons (56g) unsalted butter
  • 1/2 cup (100g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 4-6 ripe baby bananas, peeled and halved lengthwise
  • 2 tablespoons banana liqueur (optional, but enhances flavor)
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) dark rum (such as Myers's or Bacardi Black)
  • Vanilla bean ice cream, for serving

Method

  1. Prepare your serving dishes with scoops of vanilla ice cream and have them ready nearby.
  2. In a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or chafing dish set over medium heat (ideally on a portable burner for tableside preparation), melt the butter.
  3. Add the brown sugar and cinnamon to the melted butter. Stir continuously until the sugar is fully dissolved and the mixture forms a smooth, bubbling caramel sauce.
  4. Gently place the halved baby bananas into the caramel sauce, cut-side down. Cook for about 1-2 minutes per side, carefully turning them once, until they are softened and coated in the sauce.
  5. If using, pour in the banana liqueur and let it warm for about 30 seconds.
  6. Remove the skillet briefly from the heat or turn the heat to low. Carefully pour the dark rum into the skillet. Return the skillet to the heat (if removed) or gently tilt the pan towards the flame to ignite the rum. Alternatively, use a long match or lighter to ignite the rum.
  7. Allow the flames to subside naturally, shaking the pan gently. This process burns off the alcohol, leaving behind a rich, caramelized flavor. Do not lean over the pan while it is flaming.
  8. Once the flames have died down, immediately spoon the warm bananas and generous amounts of the caramel sauce over the prepared vanilla ice cream.
  9. Serve immediately and enjoy the warm, sweet, and slightly boozy dessert.

Tips

  • For safety, ensure no flammable items are near the skillet when flambéing. Have a lid handy to smother flames if needed.
  • If baby bananas are unavailable, use 2-3 regular ripe but firm bananas, sliced lengthwise or into thick rounds.
  • A pinch of nutmeg can be added with the cinnamon for an extra layer of spice.
